scope.source_policy: Current official university catalogs and official university policy or ownership pages only.
scope.variant_policy: Model the ordinary undergraduate Computer Science B.S. path. Do not merge concentrations, alternative tracks, minors, honors variants, or accelerated graduate pathways into the base degree.
scope.schedule_policy: Do not import a sample, recommended, suggested, or illustrative schedule as degree requirements. A term-organized table may be reorganized only when the institution labels it Curriculum, supplies no advisory disclaimer, uses it as the only course-level degree inventory, and its published credits close to the degree total; semester ordering is then discarded.
scope.arithmetic_policy: Preserve published ranges and overlap rules. Use a documented canonical minimum path to close the 120-credit object, and retain unsupported cross-choice logic as an explicit analysis blocker.
supersedes_findings: The partial JMU General Education description in four-year-batch-courseleaf.json; the current full catalog supplies all 14 requirements.

The blocked NSU finding in four-year-batch-courseleaf-remaining.json; a hand review determined that the institution's Curriculum table is the required 120-credit inventory, although CourseLeaf gives the table a generic Plan of Study Grid caption.

summary.analysis_blocker_policy: All three records preserve exact catalog rules that the current evaluator cannot enforce; each therefore passes catalog acceptance while failing only constraint_support for analysis readiness.

choice_rules: One of PHYS 340, ENGR 210, MATH 235, or MATH 260.
Three advanced choices from the catalog list; 495-and-above offerings may be used no more than twice.

distribution_rules: Two upper-level Writing Intensive courses are required; CPEN 371W supplies one.
Only one three-credit Area-of-Inquiry course may be in the major discipline, and no more than eight Area-of-Inquiry credits may share a discipline.

graduation.residency: 45 credits in residence; 30 of the final 36 and the final 12 major credits in residence.
graduation.upper_division_finding: No aggregate university-wide upper-division minimum is stated; the two upper-level Writing Intensive requirements and upper-level major content are modeled separately.

institutions.excluded_schedule_content: No sample or prospective schedule supplies any modeled requirement.

selected_degree.catalog_title: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science - Standard Track

ownership.college: College of Science, Engineering, and Technology

official_sources.page_scope: degree summary, required Curriculum table, and Major Electives list
40-credit General Education Core plus bachelor's graduation and residency requirements
department ownership, program list, and minimum-C rule
CSC course dictionary and credit values

curriculum_authority_decision.decision: use the course rows as degree requirements and discard their year ordering
evidence: The degree page's visible heading is Curriculum, not sample, suggested, recommended, or illustrative curriculum.
The catalog makes this table the only course-level inventory beneath the Standard Track degree.
The four published table totals are 30, 31, 28, and 31, and the table's Total Credits is 120, matching the degree's Summary of Graduation Requirements.
The catalog separately requires students to meet all requirements of the curriculum leading to the degree.
curriculum_authority_decision.caveat: CourseLeaf supplies the HTML table caption Plan of Study Grid. That generic platform caption is retained as a review flag, but there is no institutional advisory disclaimer and no competing non-sequenced course list.

degree_arithmetic.published_summary: 40 General Education + 53 Core Major + 27 Requirements Electives + 0 Other = 120.
degree_arithmetic.semantic_composition: 64 fixed computing/math/technical-writing + 8 from two distinct laboratory-science selections + 27 remaining explicit General Education + 18 upper-level CS/Math choices + 3 free elective = 120.
degree_arithmetic.general_education_overlap: The required curriculum replaces the generic CSC 150, MTH 103, and seven-credit natural-science rows with the program's computing, mathematics, and laboratory-science curriculum. Zero-increment category gates preserve the 40-credit GE obligation without double counting.
degree_arithmetic.upper_electives: The curriculum contains 18 upper-level CS-or-Math elective credits. The adjacent Major Electives authority requires at least 15 from its enumerated CSC menu, so five three-credit choices come from that menu and the final three credits may come from the menu or MATH numbered 300 or above.

graduation.residency: At least two semesters and 30 credits in residence, including all courses required by the senior-year curriculum.
graduation.department_grade_rule: Minimum C in all required English, Science, Mathematics, and Computer Science courses.
graduation.upper_division_finding: No aggregate university-wide upper-division minimum is published in the reviewed degree, General Education, department, or academic-policy sources.

blockers: the two laboratory-science sequences must be distinct
General Education substitutions overlap the fixed program curriculum
at least 15 of 18 upper elective credits must come from the enumerated CSC menu
course reuse between the two elective sections must be prevented
